description: Close gravitational encounters require smaller timesteps for accuracy, while distant particles can use larger steps. Adaptive timestepping adjusts dt based on local dynamics — either globally (shortest timescale dominates) or per-particle (block timesteps). The IAS15 integrator achieves machine-precision accuracy by adaptively choosing timesteps using a 15th-order Gauss-Radau quadrature.
mathematical_formalization: Timestep criterion: dt_i = eta * min(|v_i / a_i|, sqrt(|r_ij_min| / |a_i|)). Block timestepping: round dt_i down to nearest power of 2 fraction of the global step. Error estimator: err = |x_full - x_half| / tol.
analogical_connections: Adaptive mesh refinement in CFD: refine spatial resolution where gradients are steep
TCP congestion control: adjusts packet rate based on network conditions
Attention mechanisms in transformers: allocate more compute to important tokens
implementation_hypothesis: Start with global adaptive: estimate error by comparing full-step and two half-step results. If error > tolerance, halve dt; if error < tolerance/10, double dt.
experiment_seed: Simulate highly eccentric binary orbit (e=0.99). Compare fixed timestep vs global adaptive vs block timestep.
